headline: Aurinia keeps growing LUPKYNIS sales and profit
summary_short: Aurinia grew Q2 FY2026 revenue 7% q/q (19% y/y) to $83.2M and net income 74% y/y to $37.4M, driven by higher LUPKYNIS cartons sold to specialty pharmacies, while it closed the Kezar Life Sciences acquisition in the quarter.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $83.2M (+7% q/q, +19% y/y) on higher LUPKYNIS cartons sold to specialty pharmacies amid continued lupus nephritis market penetration, plus growth in Otsuka manufacturing-services revenue. Cost of revenue fell as fewer lower-margin LUPKYNIS units shipped to Otsuka, pushing gross margin to 92%. Operating income climbed to $46.3M and net income to $37.4M despite a higher effective tax rate (23.3% vs 2.9% a year ago, since Aurinia no longer has unused deferred tax assets to offset). R&D expense rose to fund development activity, including the May 2026 acquisition of Kezar Life Sciences. Aurinia repurchased $38.1M of shares this quarter and held $443.1M in cash and investments at quarter end, up from $398.0M at year-end 2025.

Operating cash flow rose 87% y/y to $85.1M for the six months, partially offset by $74.9M of year-to-date share repurchases.
Retained-earnings growth from net income exceeded the reduction from ongoing common-share repurchases under the Share Repurchase Plan.
Share count fell as the company repurchased shares under its Share Repurchase Plan, which has retired 23.3 million shares for $213.4 million since February 2024.
Aurinia completed its acquisition of Kezar Life Sciences on May 11, 2026, consolidating Kezar's results from that date; the filing notes results aren't necessarily indicative of future periods.

confidence_notes: No explicit numeric forward guidance (revenue/EPS range) was given; the filing offers only qualitative commentary (SG&A expected 'substantially consistent' with 2025, R&D expected to increase), so no guidance entry was added to the event shard. total_cash_usd_m ($179.73M) on the shard is a narrower balance-sheet line than the filing's broader 'cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and investments' aggregate ($443.1M vs $398.0M at year-end 2025) cited in Liquidity and Capital Resources -- both are legitimate, non-conflicting figures from the same filing, just different scopes.
